title: Dili International Marathon 2026 Review: What the 10th Edition Was Like
seo_title: Dili International Marathon 2026 Review: Course, Field, Logistics
meta_description: Dili International Marathon 2026 review: a two-lap waterfront course to Cristo Rei, 50 marathon finishers, a 2:25:51 winner, prize money for a 3:35 marathon, fees and bib collection.
dek: What it was like to run Timor-Leste's national marathon on 8 August 2026: the out-and-back waterfront course to Cristo Rei, the aid, the closed roads, a very small field with deep prize money, and what to plan before you fly to Dili.
verdict: Enter if you want a small, unhurried marathon in a country few runners visit, or a realistic shot at prize money. The 2026 race had only 50 marathon finishers and 340 in the half, on a waterfront out-and-back to Cristo Rei that the marathon runs twice, with seven water-and-medical points on the route map. Third place in the international women's category paid US$2,000 for 3:35:18. The catch is the small field and the thin information: no cut-off was published, and you may run long stretches alone on the second lap. Check the 2027 rules when they appear, and allow for bib collection, which ran only in the afternoon on two of its three days.

sections.heading: The Course: Out to Cristo Rei and Back, Twice
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes at the Nicolau Lobato Presidential Palace in Bairro Pité, and the course runs along the Dili waterfront to Cristo Rei and back [1]. The half marathon is one out-and-back [2]. On the official maps it heads north to the sea and east along Avenida de Portugal past Motael Church and Dili port, follows the shore through Lecidere and past Sant'Ana, Bekaril and Areia Branca, and turns on the headland below the Cristo Rei statue. The return uses the same road until the last 2 km, which come straight back along Avenida Nicolau Lobato to the palace [3].

The marathon map shows the same line with kilometre markers only up to 21 [3], and the timing splits, taken at 10.55 km, 21.1 km and 31.65 km, point to two laps of the half-marathon course [4]. A pre-race feature by an Australian running site says the same: the marathon uses the coastal circuit twice [5].

The organiser calls the route flat and fast, with minimal elevation change, and says it is World Athletics certified and AIMS accredited [1][2]. It was a new route for 2026, designed to show off the coastline while disrupting less city traffic [2]. The same palace-to-Cristo-Rei half-marathon course was used for the national selection race in May [6].

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The organiser's aid-station maps show seven paired water stations and medical tents on the marathon and half-marathon route: on Avenida Nicolau Lobato near the start, by the Portuguese embassy, at Sant'Ana, twice along the Metiaut shore, at Areia Branca and near the beach below Cristo Rei [3]. Because the course is an out-and-back, you pass each one going out and coming back. A separate station serves the 5 km [3].

Of a budget of about US$400,000, the organising committee said around US$300,000 would go on publicity materials, transport, and fruit and water for runners, and that every participant would get a medal [7].

No cut-off was published on the official site [2]. The slowest of the 50 marathon finishers took 5:39:14 on the gun, and the last man 5:29:51 [8]. The roads were announced closed from 5am until midday [7], so the results point to a practical limit of about six hours from the 5.30am start.

sections.heading: Roads and Race-Morning Access
paragraphs: The minister chairing the organising committee announced that public roads on the route would be closed from 5am to midday [7]. The organiser's closure map lists 20 junctions, lettered A to T, that police closed or controlled, including the Habibie Bridge roundabout and three blind bends between Areia Branca and Cristo Rei [2]. The national police said they would post officers along the course, especially in higher-risk areas, and use CCTV [7].

Avenida Nicolau Lobato and the streets around the palace close before the first start, and inside the closed area runners must walk to the start. Drivers dropping runners off were given a set approach route, with parking behind the palace [2].
The organiser said crowds lined the roads out towards Cristo Rei and back, and that people had gathered at the palace from 4am [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The marathon was won by China's Bangliu Zhang in 2:25:51, from Sardianus Sanam in 2:30:11 and Joanito Fernandes in 2:32:11 [8], the first Timorese [9]. Jiali Wang won the women's race in 2:45:24, sixth overall; the next woman finished in 3:14:29 [8]. Wang said the Timorese athletes were very strong in the early running, until the pace rose and they fell back [10].

Behind the front the field is very thin. Tenth place in the marathon was 3:16:04 for men and 4:03:13 for women, and the median finisher took 3:57:50. Only 16 of the 50 finishers were women [8]. Nine days before the race the organising committee had 1,930 registrations, 150 of them from abroad and 1,500 of them for the 5 km [7].

The half marathon is faster and deeper. Felisberto de Deus, a Timorese national-squad runner [1], won in 1:10:35 from Australia's Kieren Perkins in 1:11:05; tenth man was 1:17:32. Nefriana Ariance Daik of Indonesia won the women's race in 1:25:38 [11][9]. Perkins said the two ran together until de Deus opened a gap at about 8 km [10]. Only nine of the first 100 half-marathon finishers were women [11], and a woman quoted by the organiser said the number of women taking part was still low [12].

The prize money is large for a field this size. The organiser put the prize fund at US$77,400, split between Timorese and ASEAN+ categories, with US$4,000, US$3,000 and US$2,000 for the top three in each category of the marathon and half, and a passport or national ID needed to prove nationality [13]. Timorese runners placed fourth to tenth got between US$1,500 and US$200 [7]. In the 2026 ASEAN+ women's marathon, second place in 3:34:41 earned US$3,000 and third in 3:35:18 earned US$2,000 [9][14]. Third in the ASEAN+ men's marathon went to a runner in 3:16:04 [9].

sections.heading: Race-Week Logistics
paragraphs: Bibs and packs were collected on 5 to 7 August at the athletics federation headquarters in the GMT Building behind the National University in central Dili, with photo ID; on the Wednesday and Thursday only from 2pm to 5pm, and on the Friday also from 9am to midday [15]. Musters for the marathon, half and para race were at 4.45am [15].
In 2026 international runners paid US$90 for the marathon and US$45 for the half; Timorese runners entered free, and the 5 km needed no registration [15][2]. Entries closed on 1 August [15].

The Australian Defence Force team flew in on the Qantas direct service from Darwin [16], and Dili also has connections from Bali, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Xiamen [5]. Race week included a tree-planting ceremony on 5 August and an environmental seminar at the palace on 6 August, tied to the 2026 theme, Love Our Forests and Wildlife [7]. The race was carried live on national television [16].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a small race in a place few runners go, with a friendly national-occasion feel: the EU ambassador ran the half with an EU team [17], and Perkins said the Australian runners hoped to come back [14]. It also suits a strong club runner looking for prize money, and fields have grown: in 2025, 26 people ran the marathon and 221 the half [5].

Think twice if you need company to pace off, a published cut-off, or published entry rules. With 50 marathon finishers spread over more than three hours, expect long gaps between runners on the second lap [8].

The President announced an 11th edition for 2027, with dates and registration details to be published on the official site [1]. Nothing else about the 2027 race had been published when this was written.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information, route maps and results, the timing company's full results, and reporting in English, Portuguese and Tetum.

pull_quotes.quote: At the beginning, I ran for some time with the Timorese athletes and I found them very strong.

faqs.question: Is the Dili International Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: The organiser calls it flat and fast, with minimal elevation change. It is an out-and-back along the Dili waterfront from the Presidential Palace to the headland below Cristo Rei. The half marathon runs it once, and the timing splits show the marathon runs it twice. The organiser says it is World Athletics certified and AIMS accredited.

faqs.question: How many people run the Dili International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Very few in the long races. In 2026, 411 runners were chip-timed: 50 in the marathon, 340 in the half marathon and 21 in the 10 km para event. The free 5 km fun run was not timed. The organising committee had 1,930 registrations nine days before, 1,500 of them for the 5 km.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off at the Dili International Marathon?
faqs.answer: No cut-off was published for 2026. The slowest of the 50 marathon finishers took 5:39:14 on the gun, and the route's roads were announced closed from 5am until midday. With a 5.30am start, the results point to a practical limit of about six hours for the marathon.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to win prize money in Dili?
faqs.answer: Not as fast as elsewhere. In 2026 the organiser offered US$77,400 in prizes across Timorese and ASEAN+ categories, with US$4,000 for each category winner. Third place in the ASEAN+ women's marathon earned US$2,000 in 3:35:18, and third in the ASEAN+ men's marathon went to a runner who finished in 3:16:04.

faqs.question: What time does the Dili International Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Early. In 2026 the marathon started at 5.30am, the half marathon at 5.45am and the 10 km para race at 6am, with a 4.45am muster at the Presidential Palace. The free 5 km started at 7am. Streets around the palace close before the first start, so runners walk the last stretch.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 to the review template, about the 10th edition run on 8 August 2026. Replaces a short version built on one news report. No race-morning weather: the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive holds no observations for Dili airport (WPDL). The official site is a JavaScript app; its text, maps and results summary were read from the site's own files. The organiser's report and the timing table differ by one second on some half-marathon times; the timing table is used. TATOLI reported a US$75,000 prize fund before the race; the organiser's US$77,400 is used. No cut-off was published; the practical limit is inferred from the results and the road-closure hours. Half-marathon results beyond the first 100 were not read. No runner blogs or forum accounts of the 2026 race were found. No rating.
